source_title: Lovable vs Bolt vs Replit: who's leaking the most Supabase data?
claim_summary: Third-party scan of deployed apps: 34 of 476 scanned Lovable-hosted apps (7.1%) had a critical finding, every critical finding being Supabase row-level security (RLS) disabled on tables with user data; post updated April 24 with a larger batch; 0 of 200 YC-company control apps had a critical finding
limitation: Commercially interested source (sells the scanner); sampling frame and scanner rules not independently checked; page text is internally inconsistent (headline says 53 critical findings, table totals 64); names individual apps, which this ledger does not repeat

source_title: Claude Opus 4.7 now in Lovable
claim_summary: Opus 4.7 made available in Lovable with credits going up to 2x further until April 30; vendor benchmark versus Opus 4.6 claims 40% fewer turns, 10-20% fewer tokens, 15% faster and 2-3% higher performance
limitation: Internal benchmark not published or replicated; the changelog lists Opus 4.7 under its April 24 entry, a week after the blog date

source_title: Vibe coding upstart Lovable denies data leak, cites 'intentional behavior,' then throws HackerOne under the bus
claim_summary: Independent report: a researcher said any free account could read other users' source code, database credentials and chat histories on public projects (a BOLA flaw); Lovable first posted 'We did not suffer a data breach' and called public-project code visibility 'intentional behavior', then apologised and said HackerOne triagers had closed the reports as intended behaviour
limitation: Fetched as Claude-User (robots.txt explicitly allows it); relies on the researcher's X posts, which were not fetched; dates conflict with the vendor post (Register: private-by-default in December 2025 and researcher report about 48 days earlier with a March 3 screenshot; vendor: November 2025 and first report February 22); datePublished 2026-04-20T23:26Z while the page displays 21 Apr 00:26 UTC

source_title: Our response to the April 2026 incident
claim_summary: Vendor states that between February 3 and April 20, 2026 chat history and source code of public projects could be accessed by any Lovable user with the project link, after a February backend regression; fix shipped 'within two hours' of the April 20 public report; all current public projects being made private except official templates; first HackerOne report February 22 was closed without escalation; first public response called 'dismissive'
availability: fix stated as done; review and owner notification in progress
limitation: Vendor account; exposure scope, the number of projects viewed by others, and completion of the in-progress items are not independently verified; timeline footnote says some dates were 'incorrectly stated in original communications'

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-04-24: Security updates; Lovable desktop app; Add payments to your app (and other entries)
claim_summary: Dated entry bundles: a native macOS desktop app with local MCP server support (Windows 'coming soon'); built-in Paddle or Stripe payments for apps; SAML 2.0 SSO for apps; Business/Enterprise security updates (workspace auth policy, CSV export of secrets, audit-log improvements); new app connectors (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, BigQuery, Databricks, Snowflake and others)
availability: plan-dependent (payments on paid plans; security controls Business/Enterprise)
limitation: Changelog page is a mutable living document; one dated heading covers many items; no item exercised

source_title: Wiz findings now in Lovable
claim_summary: Native Wiz integration: when connected, Wiz scans run as part of Lovable's security suite and findings appear in the project Security view next to the built-in dependency, secrets, database and code scanners; changelog dated May 18 describes Wiz SCA and SAST
limitation: Detection quality and false-positive rates not tested; blog date (May 7) and changelog date (May 18) differ

source_title: Whitepaper: Setting the standard for agentic development
claim_summary: Standard owner reports identifying 75 coding-agent-specific risks across 13 categories with platform security teams including Lovable, Cursor, Codex and Claude Code; says Lovable is 'set to become the first' platform certified against the extended standard, with a third-party audit by Schellman scheduled for summer 2026
limitation: Co-authored with Lovable and published by the certifying body, so not independent of the certified party; the whitepaper PDF was not downloaded or read

source_title: Building is just the beginning: Introducing Discoverability
claim_summary: New apps ship as complete HTML readable by search engines and LLM crawlers; pre-rendering live across existing apps (vendor says 40 million apps already built); Semrush data built into chat; agent SEO review of sitemap, robots.txt, metadata, canonical tags and alt text; SEO Dashboard replaces the Speed Dashboard
limitation: Search ranking or traffic effects not measured; visibility is attention, not verified use

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-05-18: TanStack Start is now the default for new apps
claim_summary: New Lovable apps created from May 13, 2026 use TanStack Start with server-side rendering by default (except Enterprise, which followed on June 22); older React + Vite apps get on-request pre-rendering; the June 1 engineering post describes the move from client-rendered SPAs
limitation: Changes the dependency surface of every new generated app; see the TanStack Start advisory row (Sep 30) and the Aug 4 preview outage; upstream TanStack had a separate npm supply-chain compromise advisory on 2026-05-11 (GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx), and no Lovable statement about it was found

source_title: Turn repeated instructions into reusable skills in Lovable
claim_summary: Workspace skills: folders with a SKILL.md file plus optional supporting files, loaded on demand by description match or invoked with '/'; the vendor cites Anthropic's Skills format as portable across tools; post lists caveats (bad skills make output worse, need maintenance, changes apply only to new chats)
availability: live (workspace settings; admins and owners manage shared skills)
limitation: Portability across tools is a vendor claim not tested here; no measured effect on accepted work

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-05-18: Lovable MCP server (research preview)
claim_summary: Lovable MCP server at mcp.lovable.dev in research preview for Pro and Business, letting external clients (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and others) create projects, message the agent, inspect diffs, run SQL and deploy; June 3 entry extends it to all plans (third-party client access on by default for Free/Pro/Business, off by default on Enterprise)
availability: research preview, then all plans from 2026-06-03
limitation: Opens project write and SQL access to external clients; no permission audit performed; public GitHub repo lovablelabs/mcp (Apache-2.0, created 2026-05-13) documents the endpoint

source_title: Introducing subagents: Lovable is now better at multitasking
claim_summary: Main agent can start read-only subagents to research, explore and review a project in parallel; subagents cannot edit, create or delete files; vendor says lighter work is routed to cheaper models, often lowering the bill; changelog says available to all users
limitation: Speed and cost claims not measured

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-05-27: Sensitive data scanning
claim_summary: Enterprise workspaces can enable PII scanning across chat history, Cloud database and storage, with optional chat send protection and blocking publication of projects with unresolved PII findings
limitation: Detection accuracy not tested; Enterprise only

source_title: How Lovable protects your apps automatically
claim_summary: A background security scan (about 10 to 15 seconds) runs before publish, checking database misconfigurations, missing RLS policies and authorization gaps, with auto-fix for eligible findings; changelog defines Basic and Deep scan profiles and scheduled scans for Enterprise; a per-project security memory (May 18) records accepted risks
limitation: Auto-fix correctness not checked; accepted-risk memory can suppress repeat findings

source_title: A first look at the build economy
claim_summary: Vendor report drawing on product usage data from January 2025 to May 2026 and a May 2026 user survey; states Lovable projects average 720 million visits per month and over half of survey respondents say they are building a business
limitation: Self-reported and unaudited; survey sampling and response rate not given here; visits are not verified use; TechCrunch coverage of a revenue figure the same day was not fetched (robots.txt disallows Claude agents)

source_title: We're simplifying how billing works on Lovable
claim_summary: Separate build credits and Cloud-and-AI balances merged into a single credit balance; purchased Cloud and AI balance converted at the plan's credit price; free Cloud and AI allowances changed from dollars to 20 Cloud credits per month (plus 4 AI credits on Free); vendor says plan prices and credit costs are unchanged
feature: billing model for build plus runtime
limitation: Effect on real bills not measured; credits are not a cost per accepted task

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-06-18: Publish and install private npm packages
claim_summary: Enterprise workspaces can host a managed npm registry inside Lovable to publish internal packages (for example a shared design system) and install them in any workspace project
limitation: Entry text already uses the 'Managed registry' name that a July 30 entry says replaced 'Private registry', so dated entries are edited after publication

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-06-30: Project monitoring (Beta)
claim_summary: Project monitoring beta on Pro, Business and Enterprise: opt-in scheduled checks that review code and recent visitor errors and surface findings above chat, emailing the owner for important ones
limitation: Finding quality and noise not measured

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-07-01: Restrict who can download project code
claim_summary: Enterprise admins can disable zip code downloads so only admins and owners can download project source; does not affect connected GitHub or GitLab repositories or viewing code in the editor
limitation: Not tested

source_title: $85,000 in tokens later: What I learned from scaling agentic coding at Lovable
claim_summary: A Lovable engineer reports personal agent token spend rising from about $600 per month before joining to about $25K in May and about $85K since January, moving from plan mode and classic review (20-30 merged PRs in a productive week) to layered implementation and review agents
limitation: Single self-report; merged-PR counts are not accepted-task value; no quality or defect data

source_title: Explaining to business people why building software is still hard
claim_summary: Independent hackathon account: a team chose Lovable so recruiters could maintain the tool later, reached what felt like 90% on day one, then hit cascading bugs and slowness on day two; author uses it to argue that maintenance and design debt still dominate
limitation: One anecdote, not a controlled comparison; surfaced via a Hacker News post on 2026-09-22

source_title: Your Lovable app now works inside ChatGPT and Claude
claim_summary: Lovable apps can expose an MCP server so users can read data and take actions in the app from ChatGPT, Claude or other AI tools; August 10 changelog extends this to workspace-published apps
limitation: Exposes app actions to third-party agents; authorization model not tested

source_title: Lovable is the first coding agent platform to earn AIUC-1 certification
claim_summary: Vendor says it is the first AI coding agent platform to achieve AIUC-1 (51 requirements across six principles, with quarterly third-party red-teaming) and calls it 'independently verified, not self-attested'
limitation: No certificate, scope statement or audit report was read; the certifying body co-published with Lovable (see May 12 row); certification is not app-level security

source_title: How we run swarms of AI hacking agents against ourselves in a game of capture the flag
claim_summary: Internal offensive-security programme where swarms of AI agents attack Lovable's own platform and must capture planted flags (with no planted vulnerabilities) to prove a finding
limitation: No counts of findings or comparison with other methods were checked

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-07-25: Leaked API keys are revoked automatically
claim_summary: Workspace API keys committed to a public GitHub repository are revoked automatically after GitHub secret scanning notifies Lovable; creator and admins are emailed
limitation: Not tested

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-07-28: Upgrade an older project to TanStack Start
claim_summary: Older React + Vite projects can upgrade in place to TanStack Start via a 'Migrate to TanStack Start' action; the upgrade runs as normal chat edits that use credits, and the published site does not change until republished
availability: all projects on the older stack
limitation: Migration success rate and credit cost not measured

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-07-29: Fewer false alarms in dependency scans
claim_summary: Dependency vulnerabilities rated critical upstream but judged unable to affect Lovable apps (for example build-time-only packages) are no longer raised as findings and no longer count toward vulnerability totals
limitation: Suppression criteria are vendor judgements and were not audited

source_title: Lovable apps can now work with your users' connected tools
claim_summary: Connectors (for example Google Suite, CRMs, messaging) can now run on an app's end users' own data, not only the builder's; a companion post the same day describes how connected data is secured
limitation: Token handling and consent flows not tested

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-07-31: Opt out of AI model training
claim_summary: Users can opt out in advance: starting September 9, 2026, Lovable may use customer data from Free and Pro plans for AI model training unless the user opts out; Business and Enterprise workspace data is excluded by default; settings renamed on August 7 and the redundant workspace-level toggle removed on September 15
limitation: Terms and privacy-policy text were not read; scope of 'customer data' not checked

source_title: Previews for TanStack applications are currently unavailable
claim_summary: Status page records a full outage affecting editor, preview links and published customer sites for some active TanStack projects, from 12:27 AM to 01:52 AM on Aug 4 (about 85 minutes), resolved
limitation: Time zone not stated on the page; root cause not given; the history view only reaches back to July 2026, so April-June incidents were not screened

source_title: A dedicated security page for every business built on Lovable
claim_summary: Every published business app gets a trust-center page at its own address showing which security controls are live, read automatically by Lovable from the app
feature: public security attestation for generated apps
limitation: Shows configured controls, not tested security; reversed to off by default on Aug 17 (see that row)

source_title: Lovable + Cerebras: investing in infrastructure that keeps up with your ideas
claim_summary: Partnership with Cerebras to 'build toward dramatically reduced response times by 2027'; vendor says more than 50 million projects created since November 2024
limitation: Future target with no metric or date; the project count conflicts with the Series C post a week later (more than 60 million)

source_title: The model picker is a dead end
claim_summary: Vendor position that users should not have to pick a model; Lovable describes itself as 'model-independent' (learning how each model works best rather than treating models as interchangeable) and says it has started training its own models for routing requests, summarizing responses and writing commit messages
limitation: Opinion piece; routing quality and cost effects not shown

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-08-11: Limit on free fixes
claim_summary: Accounts get 10 free fixes (build-error 'Try to fix' and security-scan fixes) across all workspaces, each returning after 24 hours; beyond that a fix uses credits like any chat message; scans stay free
limitation: Shifts some repair cost to users; actual spend not measured

source_title: We just raised $400M in Series C funding to help people run their businesses
claim_summary: $400 million Series C at a $13.3 billion valuation led by Menlo Ventures and co-led by the Scaleup Europe Fund (EQT); vendor states more than 60 million projects and over 900 million monthly visits to Lovable-built apps; plans to grow to roughly 450 team members this year
limitation: Funding and valuation are not adoption or task value; WSJ coverage not fetched (robots.txt disallows all agents for article paths); visit figure differs from the June report (720 million)

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-08-14: Download your codebase from Git settings
claim_summary: Project code can be downloaded as a one-time .zip from Project settings -> Git without a repository connection, on paid plans for anyone with edit access
limitation: Whether exported code builds and runs outside Lovable hosting was not tested

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-08-17: Trust center is now disabled by default
claim_summary: Twelve days after launch, app trust centers became disabled by default; previously live trust pages went offline until the owner re-enables the setting
feature: public security attestation for generated apps
limitation: Reason not given; the status records a reversal of the default, not of the feature

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-08-26: Lovable works up to 10 hours on a single message
claim_summary: Lovable now works on each build message for up to 10 hours; messages are billed on work done, so long runs cost more credits; credit check-ins (beta since Aug 17) can pause a run
limitation: Cost and outcome of long runs not measured

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-08-26: Record who is behind each commit Lovable pushes
claim_summary: Business and Enterprise admins can enable recording the email address of the member whose change produced each commit Lovable pushes to GitHub or GitLab; off by default; commits Lovable makes on its own carry no address
limitation: Provenance only for opted-in workspaces; personal-data implications not assessed

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-08-31: Create a connector for any API
claim_summary: Workspace admins on any plan can create a custom connector for any REST API by describing endpoints, credentials and optional knowledge files; it then appears in the workspace catalog
limitation: Not tested

source_title: Lovable now builds with Fable 5.1
claim_summary: Lovable builds with Fable 5.1; vendor testing claims up to 17% better than Fable 5 on the hardest tasks, 31% lower cost, and a 3.5% lift in visual design quality, especially for fixing existing apps
limitation: Internal benchmark, not replicated

source_title: Introducing drafts: an easier way to collaborate and explore new ideas
claim_summary: A draft is a copy of a project with its own chat and preview; changes reach the live app only after the draft is accepted and published; first release covers front-end changes only, and drafts currently work against the published application's database
limitation: Drafts share the live database, so they are not a full staging environment; changelog dates the feature September 9; an Oct 7 status incident left projects stuck after draft merges

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-09-10: Sync your project with Bitbucket Cloud
claim_summary: Projects can sync two ways with Bitbucket Cloud: Lovable creates a private repository, pushes edits and pulls pushes back
availability: admins and owners add the connection
limitation: Not tested

source_title: Faster previews, soon powered by OJ
claim_summary: Lovable is replacing Vite in previews with OJ, its own Rust dev server; vendor claims about 4x faster cold start on a synthetic benchmark, a third to an eighth of Vite's memory, p90 dev-server time from 15.8s to 9.6s and about 6.5x less sandbox memory; around a million sandboxes a day; repository lovablelabs/oj is MIT-licensed and public
limitation: Vendor benchmarks; a Hacker News title claiming '10x' memory reduction is not supported by the post's own figures; repo created 2026-08-08, first GitHub release 2026-09-25; no energy figure is inferred

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-09-15: Skipping Lovable's questions no longer approves additional work
claim_summary: Selecting Skip on a question card now continues with reasonable defaults for the requested work and is no longer treated as approval for additional work the agent suggested
limitation: Implies that skips previously authorised extra (billable) work; how long and how often was not stated

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-09-17: Automate your workspace with the Lovable API
claim_summary: Lovable API for scripts and services: list and update projects, publish and unpublish, embed previews, and read analytics and security scans; creating a key needs Business or Enterprise and an owner or admin role
limitation: Not exercised; API changelog page also fetched but not reconciled entry by entry

source_title: Lovable acquires Sutro to make software easier to explain and easier to trust
claim_summary: Lovable acquired Sutro, whose team spent five years on a language, compiler and backend platform that make application behaviour and rules explicit, to make generated software easier to explain and trust
limitation: Terms and product integration plans not stated; no registry check of the transaction

source_title: Faster builds, same quality: Opus 5.5 now in Lovable
claim_summary: Opus 5.5 available in Lovable; vendor says it matches Opus 5 results in a third to half fewer steps and scored higher on an internal 'verification-discipline' benchmark at every effort level
limitation: Internal benchmark, not replicated; the model's vendor (Anthropic) is the maker of the assistant that prepared this ledger

source_title: Lovable + Microsoft: run the apps you build inside your company's Microsoft tenant
claim_summary: Apps built with Lovable can be published into a company's own Microsoft tenant via Copilot Managed Runtime, with the tenant's sign-in and IT controls; vendor says more than 70 million projects created
limitation: Not tested; Azure-hosted paths were not exercised (out of scope for this study's tooling)

source_title: A vulnerability in TanStack Start: what we found and what we did to protect your apps
claim_summary: Lovable says its security team found CVE-2026-102989 in TanStack Start on September 14, reported it to the maintainers, and put firewall rules in front of hosted apps; affected projects are upgraded on their next change or free via the Security page; no evidence of exploitation in reviewed logs; self-hosted deployments must patch themselves. Upstream advisory GHSA-qx66-fv34-fjm8 (published 2026-09-30) rates it critical, CVSS 3.1 score 9.3, reflected XSS, @tanstack/react-start >= 1.143.12 and < 1.168.60
availability: mitigated on Lovable hosting; patched upstream
limitation: Advisory credits list is empty, so Lovable's discovery is not corroborated there; affected-project count not given; the page title tag names the CVE while the heading does not

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-10-01: Keep your workspace's AI processing in the EU
claim_summary: Enterprise admins can enable EU inference so AI model requests run on EU providers while building and in published apps' AI features; some models and features are unavailable and the workspace uses more credits; same day, Business/Enterprise API keys can be restricted to IP allowlists; blog post on 2026-10-12
limitation: Routing not verified; credit premium not quantified

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-10-05: Restore Lovable work after a push to your Git repository replaces it
claim_summary: When a push to the synced repository replaces work Lovable made, Lovable now saves a backup and lets the project owner restore it (or keep the repository version); restored work syncs back or goes to a lovable-sync branch
limitation: Implies that before this date such pushes could overwrite Lovable-side work without a recovery path; frequency not stated

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-10-07: Cloud database changes are now recorded as Drizzle migrations
claim_summary: Lovable Cloud schema changes are now recorded as Drizzle SQL migration files under drizzle/migrations/ in the project code, and Lovable refuses changes that could break the published app such as dropping or renaming a table or column
limitation: Not tested; earlier projects' schema history before this date is not covered by the entry

source_title: Lovable changelog, 2026-10-07: Gemini 3.7 Flash is deprecated for your app's AI features
claim_summary: Gemini 3.7 Flash, made the default model for apps' AI features on August 18, is marked deprecated and stops working on January 28, 2027 because Google is retiring it; apps must switch, for example to Gemini 3.8 Flash; Gemini 3.6 Flash (default from July 22) was deprecated the day before
limitation: Event date is the announced shutdown; migration cost per app not measured

source_title: Projects stuck in Recovering acceptance after a draft merge
claim_summary: Degraded-performance incident: projects that merged a draft were stuck on 'Recovering acceptance' and could not be edited or built, from 10:19 PM to 11:46 PM on Oct 7; projects not using drafts were unaffected
limitation: Time zone not stated; number of affected projects not given
